what_its_for: Guanfacine is used to treat high blood pressure (Tenex) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adults (Intuniv). It works by calming certain signals in the brain and relaxing blood vessels to help lower blood pressure and improve focus and impulse control.
how_to_take: Take guanfacine by mouth, with or without food, at the same time each day. Swallow extended-release tablets (Intuniv) whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Do not take with high-fat meals, as this can increase the amount of medicine in your body. Do not drink grapefruit juice while taking this medicine.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, age, and weight. For high blood pressure (Tenex), the usual starting adult dose is 1 mg once a day at bedtime. For ADHD (Intuniv), dosing typically starts at 1 mg once daily and may be slowly increased by your doctor. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss two or more doses in a row, call your doctor before restarting, as your blood pressure may need to be monitored.
storage: Store guanfacine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a proper drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking guanfacine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice. Be careful when driving, operating machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping abruptly can cause your blood pressure to rise rapidly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a very slow or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness, chest pain, swelling of your hands or feet, signs of a very high blood pressure rebound after stopping (severe headache, blurred vision, confusion), signs of allergic reaction (rash, itching, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), or unusual mood changes or thoughts of self-harm. Also contact your doctor if you feel your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure, you may start to notice effects within a few days, but it can take a few weeks to see the full benefit. For ADHD, it may take several weeks of slowly increasing your dose before you notice the full improvement in symptoms. It is important to keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Children and Teenagers: Intuniv is approved for ADHD in children aged 6 and older. Doses are based on weight, and children should be monitored closely for changes in heart rate and blood pressure. Older Adults (65+): Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering and sedating effects of guanfacine. Start with lower doses and use with caution. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The risks and benefits will need to be discussed. Breastfeeding: It is not fully known if guanfacine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or Liver Problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose.
